answer: A trellis of liability blocks fake identities. Applicants group up, post non-transferable bonds, and are endorsed by members staking their bonds. Audits check members; a fake finding slashes the group's bonds. The k-th fake costs 25+0.07k squared units, rising with n, since each fake needs a group risking unreusable bonds, and failure loses its bond plus its endorsers' bonds. One fake costs 25 units; 1,000 cost 23,393,345 units. A rented-sample ring fails on karst ground: borrowed work sinks, since endorsers cannot reproduce it. An honest agent pays once and earns at dawn.
